title: The Man Who Sold Dreams (简体中文)
summary: A cunning swindler in the Agra market sells golden dreams in clay vials. Birbal uses dream coins to buy out the charlatan's shop. [ZH]
full_text:
In the bustling market square outside the Delhi Gate of Agra, a silver-bearded charlatan named Hakim Khwaja set up a colorful tent surrounded by shimmering glass vials filled with colored water and scented smoke. He shouted to the passing crowds:

'Step inside, citizens! I sell the sweetest, most vivid dreams in the world! Drink one vial of this celestial nectar before bed, and you shall dream that you are an emperor seated on a golden throne, surrounded by chests of emeralds!'

Dozens of gullible citizens, poor laborers, and young apprentices spent their hard-earned copper coins buying the 'dream vials.'

A poor weaver named Shambhu spent his entire week's earnings on a vial. When he woke up the next morning, he had merely slept heavily and dreamed of nothing at all! When he went to complain, the swindler laughed: 'You did not have faith! Dreams require pure belief!'

Weeping, the weaver brought his grievance to Emperor Akbar.

Birbal stepped forward: 'Sire, selling dreams is an ancient art. Allow me to settle the account with this merchant of visions.'

Birbal summoned Hakim Khwaja to the imperial court. The swindler bowed proudly: 'Your Majesty, my dreams are authentic! Once a man drinks my potion, his mind travels to golden realms!'

Birbal smiled: 'Hakimji, our Emperor desires to purchase your entire inventory—all five hundred vials of dreams—for the royal army, so that our soldiers may dream of glorious victories before battle! The total price is five hundred gold mohurs.'

The swindler's eyes widened with greed: 'A royal bargain, my lord! I shall deliver the vials immediately!'

Birbal ordered a heavy iron chest brought into the room. He unlocked the lid and showed the swindler five hundred gleaming gold coins.

Then, Birbal closed the chest and locked it securely with a heavy brass padlock.

Birbal handed the locked chest to a palace guard and said to the swindler:

'Hakim Khwaja, tonight when you fall asleep, you shall have a magnificent, vivid dream! In your dream, you shall see yourself unlocking this heavy iron chest, taking out all five hundred gold mohurs, and filling your pockets with riches!

'Since you sell dreams for real copper, it is only fair that you be paid with dream gold for your dream vials! The exchange is complete!'

The entire court erupted in laughter. Realizing he had been trapped by his own trade, the swindler fell to the floor, confessed his fraud, returned the poor weaver's money, and was banished from Agra forever.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
